# Fix deleting a board with tasks raising activity_log_board_id_fkey (M7 task activity trigger), continuing Hermes's handoff.

%% generated by scripts/obsidian-sync.ts: edit the sources, not this file %%

**Tasks:** [[tasks/PSI-107|PSI-107]] · **Agent:** claude-code · **Operator:** ardian · **Outcome:** partial

**Session:** 2026-09-28 13:00 WIB → 2026-09-28 13:45 WIB · branch `task/PSI-107`

**Human review:** required: db_reset and db_tests could not be executed in this sandbox (no Docker). Needs a real pgTAP run before status can move past doing/review.

## Summary

Root cause: `delete from boards` cascades to `tasks` (board_id on delete cascade), firing the tasks_activity AFTER DELETE trigger per row. log_task_activity() inserted an activity_log row with board_id = old.board_id, but by the time the tasks cascade runs, the boards row is already gone, so the insert violates activity_log_board_id_fkey. Added new migration 20260928062634_fix_task_activity_board_delete.sql (M7 itself untouched, C-06) that re-creates log_task_activity() with a guard: in the DELETE branch, if the board no longer exists (not exists check against public.boards) the inserted board_id is nulled instead of raising; INSERT/UPDATE branches unchanged. Added 2 new pgTAP cases to supabase/tests/activity_log.test.sql (plan 9 -> 11): #9 lives_ok on deleting a board with a column and task, #10 confirms a task delete on a still-live board still logs with board_id populated. Could not execute db_reset/test db in this session: Docker Desktop's engine pipe is unreachable in this remote sandbox (`supabase db reset` fails immediately trying to reach dockerDesktopLinuxEngine), so the migration and new pgTAP assertions are unverified by an actual run. Everything else (task claim, branch, migration, test) is in place; marking partial pending a real `supabase db reset && supabase test db` pass in an environment with Docker.

## Decisions

- **Null board_id on the deleted-task activity row instead of skipping the insert entirely**: Accept criteria explicitly allows either; nulling keeps a 'deleted' audit trail entry for the task even when its board vanished in the same statement, whereas skipping would silently drop it. board_id is nullable already.
- **New migration re-creates the whole log_task_activity() function rather than a partial patch**: C-06 forbids editing the applied M7 migration; `create or replace function` is the standard way to ship a follow-up fix without a second trigger object, and it keeps the function body diffable against the M7 doc.
